summary: In a mall scene, a police officer named Arturo confronts a security guard after robots have been destroyed and electronics fried. Arturo flashes his badge, takes the guard's pepper spray, and sees his phone, sidearm and the guard's devices all disabled by what appears to be infowar equipment. The R Peed unit Ada had led there was fried, and the guard threatens to report Arturo. The passage is a fragment from a larger fiction novel, Book 4, part 56.
one_line: Arturo, a police officer, clashes with a security guard amid a mall full of fried robots and dead electronics.
key_facts: Arturo flips his badge and shows it to a security guard, speaking in what the note calls his cop-voice.
The guard has an Oceanic twang, a accent Arturo has been hearing more as crowded South Pacific islands boil over UNATS.
A pile of dead robots lies before them: both R Peed units, a pair of mall-sweepers, a flying cambot, and a squat octopus-armed maintenance robot.
A sweeper bot grabs the maintenance bot by a fine manipulator, and the guard tells it to stop, and the robot second-lawed to a halt.
Arturo thumbs the backup number into his phone, wanting more real cops on the scene fast.
A crack-bang sound and dimming lights disable the sweeper bot, which lies on the ground.
Arturo's phone screen has gone charred black and its idiot lights are out; its battery is hot enough to raise a blister on his fingertip.
The security guard says his own gear is dead too: cash registers, bots, and credit-cards.
Arturo's UNATS Robotics sidearm, which has a snitch-brain recording when, where and how it is drawn, is frozen in place and dead.
Arturo demands the guard's pepper spray and truncheon, and takes the pepper spray from the guard's hand.
The guard refuses at first, saying losing them would cost his job, then says he has Arturo's bloody badge number and witnesses.
Ada had led the first R Peed unit to the mall, and it was fried by very ugly infowar equipment.
